tools.name: scan_situations
tools.description:
Run the deterministic target-specific scanner over EventsUnified and return ranked
historical situation envelopes. Prefer this first for open-ended orientation; it
covers the replay's known correlated patterns without model-authored KQL.

start.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window start.

end.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window end, no more than 48 hours later.

tools.name: get_situation_evidence
tools.description:
Return bounded EventsUnified rows cited by one deterministic scanner situation.
Call after scan_situations when the question asks why a situation exists; do not
replace this with arbitrary KQL.

start.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window start.

end.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window end, no more than 48 hours later.

tools.name: profile_host_activity
tools.description: Return a bounded categorical product/event-type profile for one observed host. Prefer this for host activity composition before considering raw KQL.

start.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window start.

end.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window end, no more than 48 hours later.

tools.name: get_authentication_activity
tools.description: Return bounded categorical Windows authentication activity for one host. Prefer this for logon success/failure, account, and source questions; it covers event ids 4624, 4625, and 4648.

start.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window start.

end.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window end, no more than 48 hours later.

tools.name: get_privileged_session_activity
tools.description: Return bounded categorical CyberArk privileged-session records for one host. Prefer this for session, privileged access, and window-title evidence; text is truncated by the ADX boundary.

start.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window start.

end.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window end, no more than 48 hours later.

tools.name: get_dns_activity
tools.description: Return bounded categorical DNS activity for one observed source address. Prefer this for domain, cadence, and DNS-volume questions before considering raw KQL.

start.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window start.

end.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with UTC offset; window end, no more than 48 hours later.

tools.name: search_mitre_attack
tools.description:
Search pinned MITRE ATT&CK knowledge in Azure AI Search: the analytics and detection
strategies of one pinned enterprise-attack bundle. Use it to characterise a situation the
scanner already produced — pass the situation's technique ids or behaviour class as
filters and the analyst question as free text. Results are advisory ATT&CK context with
provenance, never a verdict and never proof that replayed activity was malicious. It reads
no telemetry, so it never replaces the telemetry tools.

question.description: Analyst question in free text; ranks the filtered set. May be empty.

technique_ids.description: ATT&CK ids such as T1087.002. Empty array applies no technique filter.

behaviour_classes.description: Closed behaviour vocabulary carried by scanner factors. Empty array applies no behaviour filter.

platforms.description: ATT&CK platforms such as Windows or Linux. Empty array applies no platform filter.

tools.name: record_situation_diagnosis
tools.description:
Record the final plain-language diagnosis of one situation. Call this exactly once, only after
gathering evidence with the other tools. The headline must read as a sentence an analyst would say
out loud about what appears to be happening, naming the host, account, and activity. Describe the
historical replay in the past tense. Never claim live monitoring, prevention, containment, or a
confirmed breach.

headline.description: One sentence naming what appears to be happening, on which host, by which account.

narrative.description: Two to four sentences: the sequence observed, why it fits together, and what it would mean.

assessment.description: How strongly the gathered evidence supports intrusion-like activity.

supporting_observations.description: Each entry states one observed fact and the tool or count it came from.

would_change_the_call.description: Facts not established here that would raise or lower the assessment.

evidence_ids.description: resource_id values seen in tool output that support the headline.

situation_type.description: The closest situation type: copy verbatim the title of one MITRE ATT&CK document search_mitre_attack returned in this run. Never invent a label.

citation_ids.description: doc_id values of MITRE ATT&CK documents search_mitre_attack returned in this run, starting with the one naming situation_type.

tools.name: record_sequence_step
tools.description:
Record ONE step of the sequence of events, then call this again for the next step. Push the
steps one at a time in chronological order, earliest first, starting at position 1. Each step is
one short past-tense line naming the account or host and what it did. Take the timestamp verbatim
from telemetry a tool returned in this run; leave it empty rather than estimating one. evidence_ids
must be resource_id or doc_id values that a tool in THIS run returned, and only the ones that
support THIS step — the server resolves them against what the tools actually returned and marks
anything else unsupported. Never claim live monitoring, prevention, containment, or a confirmed
breach.

position.description: 1-based position of this step in chronological order.

description.description: One short past-tense line: who or what, and what happened. No JSON, no tool output.

timestamp.description: The step's time copied verbatim from tool output, or an empty string if telemetry gave none.

evidence_ids.description: resource_id or doc_id values a tool returned in this run that support this step; may be empty.

tools.name: complete_sequence_of_events
tools.description:
Close the sequence of events. Call this exactly once, after the last record_sequence_step call,
and then stop. It records nothing but what is uncertain about the ordering.

ordering_note.description: What is uncertain about the ordering, or an empty string if it is fully established by timestamps.

tools.name: query_events_kql
tools.description:
LAST-RESORT FALLBACK: run one bounded, read-only model-authored KQL pipeline rooted
at EventsUnified. Use only when no purpose-built tool covers the analyst's actual
question. Never use it merely to reproduce scanner, situation evidence, host,
authentication, privileged-session, or DNS activity tools. Explain the uncovered
shape in the query's purpose through projected categorical fields.

query.description: One read-only EventsUnified KQL pipeline for a shape not covered by a purpose-built tool.
